statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail eases within the low band: NQ has retraced roughly 82 points from a fresh 29,764.25 overnight high instead of holding it, and the index complex is openly split with YM down 0.65% against NQ up 0.40%, while Stress stays at the top of the elevated band on a third day of crude gains.
recommendation: The deterministic Tail-to-action mapping resolves to EA_ON for NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD alike. A narrow danger window remains flagged for the post-holiday U.S. cash reopening between 13:30 and 15:00 UTC, where a single auction discounts two sessions of accumulated Gulf, energy and rates news. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: NQ rejects a fresh 29,764.25 overnight high while Dow futures fall 0.65% and a third day of crude gains keeps Stress at the top of the elevated band
body: U.S. cash equity markets were closed on Monday 7 September for Labor Day and reopen at 13:30 UTC today, so the Nasdaq-100 last settled a full cash session on 4 September. NQ futures trade at 29,682.25, up 117.00 points or 0.40% from the 29,565.25 previous close, inside an overnight band of 29,525.00-29,764.25. The material change since the previous assessment is that the fresh high has been rejected: NQ tagged 29,764.25 and has since retraced roughly 82 points, so the session-extreme hold flagged an hour ago is no longer present. That is the opposite of the pathological pattern, and it arrives without any shallow-pullback sequence, failed-retracement chain or repeated extension. Cross-asset confirmation is not merely absent but actively contradictory, and the contradiction has widened. Dow futures are at 53,092.00, down 348.00 points or 0.65%, in a 53,042.00-53,336.00 band, and S&P 500 e-mini futures are at 7,715.75, down 0.08%, between 7,698.50 and 7,728.50. Three U.S. index futures now disagree on direction with the widest spread of the overnight session. The Asian session explains the split. Reuters reports the Nikkei 225 up 0.2% and MSCI's Asia-Pacific ex-Japan index up 0.2% led by a 1.2% gain in the Kospi, with the yen jumping as much as 0.6% to 153.51, its strongest since 18 February, ahead of the 17-18 September Bank of Japan meeting. The latest available cash-session sector picture is consistent with that: technology higher, communication services and consumer cyclicals lower, and semiconductors leading. This is a chip and technology bid rather than an index-wide directional bid, which is precisely why the Nasdaq-100 can rise while the Dow falls. Rates are not the pressure point in this window. The 10-year sits near 4.78% and the 2-year at 4.37%, with the two available reads disagreeing only on whether the day's change is marginally positive or negative, and the dollar index is around a two-week low of 98.82. The VIX reference of 15.30 predates the holiday and is a stale last-cash-session print rather than live evidence, which is one of the reasons Confidence is held below the top of its band. The Stress side carries the risk. Brent is at $97.76, up 1.54%, and WTI at $93.14, up 1.81%, a third consecutive day higher after the weekend exchange of strikes in the Strait of Hormuz in which the U.S. hit three Iranian tankers, the IRGC claimed strikes on three tankers and three U.S.-linked vessels, and Saudi Aramco's Jizan refinery was struck for the second time in a month. Iran has since threatened to retaliate against further attacks by targeting energy infrastructure across the Gulf, including U.S. oil and gas interests. That threat is unretracted and keeps an overnight gap channel open, but a threat is not an observed price path, and the crude move has so far transmitted into inflation expectations rather than into Nasdaq-100 trend structure. The calendar today is light: NFIB Business Optimism at 10:00 UTC, NY Fed Consumer Inflation Expectations at 15:00 UTC, the 3-year note auction at 17:00 UTC and Consumer Credit at 19:00 UTC, with PPI on 10 September and CPI on 11 September the week's high-impact prints. The narrow danger window between 13:30 and 15:00 UTC is retained because the reopening auction has to discount two sessions of accumulated Gulf, energy and rates news in a single print, which is a structural gap risk rather than an observed one. Shared Finviz cross-asset context was read but is roughly three hours old and therefore stale under the applicable freshness rule; it was used only for headline discovery and latest-session sector colour, and every material story behind this assessment was verified against primary reporting. Tail is scored at 7 on observed two-way trade, an explicit rejection of the overnight high and the widest index-futures disagreement of the session. Stress is held at 64, at the top of the elevated band, on the unresolved energy and geopolitical channel and the information-dense reopening. Confidence is 84 on fresh futures, yield, crude and currency reads and verified reporting, discounted for the stale VIX print and stale shared context.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry a published Claude assessment and every one of them mapped to EA_ON. Tail sat at 5-7 through the European and early U.S. hours of 7 September, stepped to 9-10 around the 14:00 and 16:00 UTC windows, fell back to 5 into the evening, then settled into a persistent 8-10 range from 22:00 UTC onward as the overnight NQ advance developed. Stress rose from the mid-50s to a stable 62-64 once the weekend Gulf escalation and the crude move were priced, and Confidence recovered from 75 to 84 as live futures evidence displaced the holiday-thinned reads. Dominant mode alternated between normal and mixed and never resolved to a trend label.
outlookSummary: The projection holds Tail inside the low band across all 24 hours, with a shallow rise into the post-holiday U.S. cash reopening and a peak of 14 in the 14:00 UTC hour that still maps to EA_ON. The rise is conditional structural risk from an unusually information-dense reopening auction, not an assertion that a directional path has been observed. Stress runs 62-67, highest across the U.S. session, on the unresolved Gulf energy channel. Confidence decays from 84 to 70 with distance from the evidence. The stated invalidations are a reclaim of 29,764.25 without any retracement, a European-led break below 29,525.00, or repeated extension after failed retracements once U.S. cash trades; any of those would justify a materially higher Tail than projected here.

forecast.analysis: NQ trades 29,682.25, +0.40%, after tagging a fresh 29,764.25 overnight high and retracing about 82 points. That rejection removes the session-extreme hold flagged an hour ago. YM is -0.65% and ES -0.08%, so the index complex is openly split. Tail eases within the low band.

forecast.analysis: Asia hands over to the European pre-open with Tokyo and Seoul cash shut. Liquidity thins, which widens the overnight band without establishing direction. Tail is held on the assumption that 29,764.25 is not reclaimed on a one-way push; a decisive break with no pullback would be the invalidation.

Checkpoint: whether 29,764.25 is reclaimed without a retracement
Yen at 153.51, a six-month high, still weighing on Japanese exporters

forecast.analysis: European cash markets open. The reaction there to a third day of rising crude is the first live read on whether the energy channel is being treated as an equity problem. Tail nudges up for the open, conditional on the overnight band holding; a European-led break through 29,525.00 would change the read.

Overnight NQ band 29,525.00-29,764.25 is the reference for the open

forecast.analysis: First full European hour in this projection. Stress edges up because European energy and rates pricing usually sets the tone the U.S. reopening inherits. Tail stays low: nothing observed supports a no-retracement path, and the assumed NQ-versus-YM split keeps capping directional conviction.
drivers: European rates and energy pricing set the tone the U.S. session inherits
Assumed persistence of the NQ-versus-YM split caps directional conviction
Stress raised on the unresolved Gulf energy channel

forecast.analysis: Mid-morning Europe, the last window in which positioning is set without American cash flow. The Tail step reflects a modest build into the reopening rather than any observed extension. A dollar index near a two-week low of 98.82 is a mild offset to the crude-driven inflation channel.
drivers: Mid-morning Europe: positioning set before U.S. cash flow returns
Dollar index near 98.82, a two-week low, partly offsetting crude strength
Tail build reflects the approaching reopening, not observed extension

forecast.analysis: NFIB Business Optimism for August prints at 10:00 UTC. It is a second-tier survey that rarely moves the index on its own, so it is carried as a checkpoint rather than a Tail driver. Scores are unchanged from the prior hour; only a large miss alongside a crude extension would warrant more.
drivers: Checkpoint: NFIB Business Optimism Index (Aug) at 10:00 UTC
Second-tier survey, historically not an index-level mover by itself
Escalation path would require a large miss plus a crude extension

forecast.analysis: European afternoon, roughly two and a half hours before the U.S. cash reopening. Volume typically rebuilds here as American desks come in. Tail is held flat; the meaningful change is expected in the next hour, once pre-open flow starts discounting two sessions of Gulf and rates news.
drivers: European afternoon: U.S. desks return and volume rebuilds
Two sessions of accumulated news still to be discounted at the reopen
Tail held pending pre-open order flow rather than raised in advance

forecast.analysis: U.S. pre-market hour. The Nasdaq-100 last settled a full cash session on 4 September, so the reopening auction has an unusually large backlog to price. The Tail lift covers that conditional structural risk from the holiday gap; it is not an observation that a directional path has formed.
drivers: U.S. pre-market: last full cash settlement was 4 September
Holiday backlog makes the reopening auction unusually information-dense
Tail lift is conditional on gap structure, not on observed extension
Third-day crude strength remains the dominant cross-asset input

Tail peaks here as conditional opening-structure risk; whether pullbacks are shallow can only be scored once it trades.

Tail sits at its 24-hour maximum to cover the extension branch; an early two-way range with genuine retracements would justify a quick reduction.

Second half of the 13:30-15:00 UTC danger window

If instead the morning produced repeated extension after failed retracements, this is the slot where a low reading would prove wrong.

Step-down assumes orderly morning price discovery

forecast.analysis: The 3-year note auction at 17:00 UTC is the first of three coupon sales this week and the first demand test with the 2-year at 4.37%. A weak stop would push yields up into the equity afternoon. Tail is held as a supply checkpoint rather than as a directional call.

forecast.analysis: Post-auction hour. With the supply event assumed cleared, Tail eases while Stress holds, because the crude and Gulf backdrop is unresolved regardless of how the auction goes. Nothing in this slot is observed; it inherits whatever structure the afternoon actually builds.
drivers: Post-auction hour: the supply event is assumed cleared
Stress held on the unresolved Gulf energy backdrop

forecast.analysis: Consumer Credit for July prints at 19:00 UTC and the final cash hour begins. Power hour can produce late continuation or a sharp reversal, so Tail ticks back up. The July credit series is low-impact and is carried as a calendar checkpoint, not as a driver of the path.

Final cash hour: late continuation or sharp reversal both plausible
Tail tick-up covers the reversal branch, not an observed trend

forecast.analysis: U.S. cash closes at 20:00 UTC. Index-level path risk normally decays immediately as closing imbalances clear and volume falls away, so Tail and Stress both step down. The first post-holiday session will by then have set the reference range the overnight market trades against.
drivers: U.S. cash close at 20:00 UTC: closing imbalances clear
Index-level path risk normally decays as volume falls away
First post-holiday session sets the overnight reference range

forecast.analysis: Post-close hour ahead of the futures maintenance break. Liquidity is at its thinnest of the 24-hour cycle and directional structure rarely survives it, which is why the projected mode is normal. The quiet does not resolve the underlying energy and rates questions.
drivers: Post-close hour ahead of the futures maintenance break
Thinnest liquidity of the cycle; directional structure rarely persists
A quiet window does not resolve the energy or rates questions

forecast.analysis: Globex reopens for the 9 September session. Reopening prints on thin books can look impulsive without carrying information, which is exactly the pattern that should not be read as trend. Gulf headline risk keeps an overnight gap channel open through this window.

Impulsive thin-book prints should not be read as trend
Gulf headline risk keeps an overnight gap channel open

That relaxation is explicitly conditional: a fresh strike, or an actual move against Gulf energy infrastructure, would reverse it immediately.
